title: Off-grid solar in Sub-Saharan Africa: the multi-gigawatt opportunity hiding in plain sight | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie forecasts Sub-Saharan Africa's installed off-grid solar PV will grow sixfold by 2035, driven by expensive diesel (especially in post-subsidy Nigeria), cheap imported modules and mining demand in the DRC. Demand is not in doubt; the binding constraint is financing, with currency depreciation and double-digit rates keeping capital costs high.

insights.claim: 600 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa still lack reliable electricity because national grids have not kept pace with population growth, leaving off-grid solar PV as the region's main electrification engine.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Large unserved demand base supports distributed solar developers and solar-as-a-service models in the region.
insights.locator: Six hundred million people across Sub-Saharan Africa

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie forecasts total installed off-grid solar PV in Sub-Saharan Africa will grow sixfold (about 450%) by 2035, driven by costly diesel, cheap modules and new private financing.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: A multi-GW growth market for module suppliers, storage and distributed energy financiers through 2035.
insights.quote: diesel that has become too expensive to run, modules that have become too cheap to ignore, and private capital that is learning to finance the gap
insights.locator: Off-grid solar PV is quietly becoming

insights.claim: Nigeria will account for close to 35% of Sub-Saharan off-grid solar installations by 2035, because since the 2023 fuel-subsidy removal diesel self-generation has become so expensive that solar-as-a-service undercuts it.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Nigeria is the anchor market for C&I off-grid solar developers; subsidy policy is the key swing factor.
insights.locator: Nigeria alone accounts for close to 35%

insights.claim: For Nigerian commercial and industrial users, displacing even a quarter of load with solar delivers immediate savings, and many developers supply the system at no upfront cost.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Zero-capex service models shift balance-sheet and currency risk onto developers and their financiers.
insights.locator: For a commercial or industrial user

insights.claim: Kenya, the continent's most mature off-grid market, is shifting from first-time access toward cost optimisation as net-metering rules and grid extension take hold.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Kenyan off-grid growth becomes commercially driven and grid-competitive, lowering the access-driven volume upside.

insights.claim: The Democratic Republic of Congo will be an off-grid solar leader thanks to one of the continent's strongest mining-linked solar pipelines.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Miners replacing on-site fossil generation offer a bankable, large-ticket off-grid solar-plus-storage segment.
insights.locator: Mining is turning the DRC and the copper belt

insights.claim: As of summer 2026 the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex is served by an integrated 233 MWdc solar-and-storage facility delivering guaranteed baseload power, showing renewables can displace diesel in heavy industry.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: A reference project for solar-plus-storage baseload at mines; watch for copies across the copper belt.
insights.quote: renewable baseload that competes with and displaces diesel in heavy industry

insights.claim: Sub-Saharan markets excluding South Africa have imported over 27 GWdc of solar modules since 2022, and falling module costs keep the affordability case strong through the decade.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Module import data points to a far larger installed distributed base than official statistics may capture; a demand outlet for module exporters.

insights.claim: Value stacking (layering finance, appliances and services onto the energy sale) is turning off-grid solar from a product into a platform business and making more deployments bankable.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Favour off-grid operators with multi-revenue platform models over pure hardware sellers.

insights.claim: Financing is the binding constraint on Sub-Saharan off-grid solar: currency depreciation and double-digit interest rates keep capital costs high, and inconsistent rural-electrification policy is a persistent drag.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: FX-hedging, blended finance and local-currency lending providers are the gatekeepers of how much growth happens.
insights.locator: However, financing remains the binding constraint

insights.claim: How much of the multi-gigawatt opportunity is realised will depend on emerging private and blended-finance models bridging the funding gap, not on demand, which is not in doubt.
insights.speaker: Sohan  Gwalani
insights.so_what: Track DFI/blended finance vehicles as the leading indicator for regional off-grid volumes.
insights.quote: will depend not on demand, which is not in doubt, but increasingly on the private and blended-finance models emerging to bridge the funding gap
insights.locator: How much of this multi-gigawatt opportunity is realised
